t: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
h: An unwanted orphan learns he is a wizard and gets a castle, a school and two best friends; cozy, inventive and built for rereading.

like.t: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
like.r: Another ordinary child steps into a hidden magical world, in a shorter, more allegorical story with a quieter kind of wonder.
A kid finds out he belongs to a secret magical world, with the same school-year rhythm but Greek gods and a wisecracking narrator.

like.t: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
like.r: The faithful screen version keeps nearly every beat and makes the castle and its candlelit halls something you can walk through.

t: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
h: The series turns darker and cleverer as an escaped prisoner stalks the school and old loyalties are rewritten; a fan favorite for its tight plot.

like.r: A child-led fantasy with real menace and moral weight, aimed at readers ready for something darker than a school story.
The quieter, older ancestor of the wizard-school story, where magic costs something and growing up means facing your own shadow.

like.t: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
like.r: The most stylish film of the series, with a looser, moodier look that matches the book's darker turn.

t: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
h: The school year is gone and three exhausted friends hunt through a wartime Britain for the pieces of a villain; a long, grim, emotional finale.

like.r: Another long quest ending in sacrifice, with a wider cast and a more mythic, less personal sense of dread.
A fast, brutal story of teenagers pushed into a war they did not choose, with no school-story comforts to soften it.

like.t: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
like.r: A big-screen finale of the same kind, with long marches, impossible odds and a payoff built over many hours.

h: A teenage hunter takes her sister's place in a televised fight to the death; propulsive, brutal and sharp about spectacle and hunger.

like.r: The grown-up, far bloodier cousin: a class of students forced to kill each other, with much less hope and much more gore.
The classic of state power and surveillance behind this story's world, told for adults and without any rescue.
A tense, handheld screen version with a strong lead performance that keeps the book's satire of reality television.

h: A fierce girl crosses a parallel Europe to rescue stolen children, with armored bears, witches and a daring argument about the church.

like.r: Another thoughtful, shadow-haunted fantasy where power has a price, written in a plainer, more fable-like voice.

like.t: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
like.r: The cozier, more Christian counterpart: the same children-in-another-world frame, which Pullman partly set out to argue with.
The film version trades the book's theology for spectacle but gives the daemons and the armored bears a lavish look.

h: In a Chicago sorted into five factions, a girl who fits none of them trains with brutal rivals while a quiet coup builds.

like.r: The template for this kind of story: sharper, bloodier and more grounded in a hungry, unequal world.
The quieter, shorter ancestor of the sorted-society dystopia, where one child slowly sees what the system hides.
A cool, thoughtful film about a society that sorts people by birth and the one person who refuses his category.

h: A boy wakes with no memory in a glade of other boys ringed by a shifting stone maze; short chapters and a steady drip of puzzles.

like.r: The darker, more literary version of boys building a society alone, where the community frays instead of rallying.
Another teen survival story run by unseen adults, with more emotional depth and a sharper view of who is watching.
A fast, clean film version that turns the maze itself into a chase through collapsing walls.

h: A new girl in a rainy town falls hard for a pale, protective classmate with a secret; swoony, obsessive and enormously readable.

like.r: The lush, adult, tragic take on vampire longing that made the genre sexy, with far more blood and philosophy.
The older model for a prickly pair circling each other across a gap in class and temperament, with wit instead of fangs.
The moody, blue-gray film version, where the Pacific Northwest weather does as much for the romance as the leads.

h: Two teenagers with cancer fall in love over a book and a trip to Amsterdam; funny and well read, and built to make you cry.

like.r: Another sharp, funny teen love story that treats its young leads as smart people and keeps the pain close by.

like.t: Me and Earl and the Dying Girl
like.r: A snarkier, more self-mocking take on a teen facing a friend's illness, deliberately avoiding the tearjerker route.
A warm, closely faithful film with two lead performances that carry the book's banter and its heartbreak.

h: A boy goes to boarding school to seek a great perhaps and meets a wild, unforgettable girl; funny first, then devastating.

like.t: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
like.r: Another sensitive narrator finding friends and facing hidden pain, told through letters and more openly about trauma.
The original prep-school misfit voice, older and angrier, in the same hunt for something real among phonies.
Boarding-school friends swept up by one charismatic person and then broken by a loss, with the same mix of joy and grief.

h: A foster girl steals books in Nazi Germany while Death himself narrates; warm, strange and quietly devastating.

like.t: The Boy in the Striped Pajamas
like.r: Another Second World War story seen through a child, shorter and starker, and built around one painful gap in understanding.

like.t: The Diary of a Young Girl
like.r: The real voice behind so many stories like this one: a teenager hiding in the war and writing to stay alive.
Another tale of a family trying to keep its humor and tenderness in the shadow of the Holocaust.

h: In a calm society with no pain and no choices, a boy is chosen to hold its forgotten memories; spare, unsettling and quickly read.

like.r: Another short story of a controlled, contented society, where a single person starts to see what has been taken away.
A livelier, more action-driven teen story about a smoothed-over society and the one girl who starts questioning it.
A man discovers his perfect, comfortable world has been arranged for him, and must decide whether the truth is worth the cost.

h: A farm boy finds a dragon egg and sets out with an old storyteller on a classic quest; familiar, sincere and big on dragons.

like.r: The source of so much of this book's map and spirit, lighter in tone and shorter, with a more playful narrator.
The great story of bonded dragons and riders, told in a more adult science-fantasy setting.
A lively animated take on a young person bonding with a dragon, with more humor and a lighter touch.

h: An unremarkable mapmaker turns out to hold a rare power that could free a darkened land; brooding, Russian-flavored and romantic.

like.r: A similarly Eastern European-flavored fantasy about a girl, a brooding sorcerer and a spreading darkness, with more folklore.
Another teen-led fantasy of deadly courts and a powerful young woman, with more romance and a faster hook.
A strong, guarded heroine with a dangerous gift in a richly built kingdom, written with the same serious tone.

h: Six teenage outcasts try one impossible job in a city of thieves; a clever, banter-heavy heist with real scars underneath.

like.r: The grown-up version of the same crew-of-thieves set-up, with grimier streets, nastier humor and longer cons.
The slick model for a heist told through a gang of specialists, minus the magic and the trauma.
The earlier tale in the same world, slower and more romantic, which sets up the lands the crew moves through.

h: A teenage assassin is pulled from a prison mine to compete for the king's champion; deadly tournaments, court secrets and a love triangle.

like.r: A lethal young woman with a gift she hates, in a kingdom of cruel kings, with a slower and more thoughtful pace.
Another deadly contest with a hard-edged young heroine, set in a bleak future rather than a castle.
A fairy-tale heroine with a hidden past and a prince at court, lighter in tone and set among androids.

t: A Court of Thorns and Roses
h: A hunter kills a wolf, is dragged into a faerie court and falls for her captor; swoony, spicy and built on Beauty and the Beast.

like.r: The tale this book is built on, in a sweeter and funnier telling, without the steam or the slow-building war.
A gentler, quieter retelling of the same fairy tale, centered on the heroine's gradual affection.
Another dangerous faerie court and a mortal girl who learns the rules, with a sharper, more vengeful heroine.

h: A girl from a family of psychics joins four prep-school boys hunting a sleeping Welsh king; dreamy, strange and lyrical.

like.r: A darker, adult story of devoted friends bound by a shared obsession at an elite school, with more dread.
A quiet family story of women with real magic and real sorrow, set in a New England town.
A group of prep-school friends who find something larger than school together, only the tone is far more earthbound.

h: A sixteen-year-old witnesses a police shooting of her friend and must decide whether to speak; angry, funny and full of family warmth.

like.r: The older American classic about race and justice through a young narrator, quieter and more reflective.
A shorter, similarly urgent teen novel about a boy confronting racism and police violence, told with letters.
A hot summer day on one Brooklyn block builds to a flashpoint, making the same point with more heat and less comfort.

t: The Absolutely True Diary of a Part-Time Indian
h: A cartoon-loving teen leaves his reservation school for an all-white one; funny, blunt and raw about poverty, grief and belonging.

like.r: The older outsider-teen voice that this book echoes, though it is far more privileged and less tied to community.
Another candid, funny memoir in comics about family pain and finding yourself, from an adult looking back.
A teen narrator caught between two worlds and two communities, told with the same candor and humor.

t: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
h: A shy freshman writes letters about new friends, mix tapes and a past he cannot quite name; tender, awkward and very sad.

like.r: The classic fragile, observant narrator, more bitter and funnier than this gentler, more grateful voice.
Another school story of a bookish boy and a group of friends who change him, with more wit and a hard loss.
A group of teenage misfits finds understanding in one another, in a shorter and less painful setting.

h: Two misfits fall for each other on a 1986 school bus through comics and mix tapes; funny, tender and honest about a hard home.

like.r: Another bright, bookish teen romance with a clear sense of what is at stake, set in the present day.
A sweetly earnest film about two mismatched teenagers falling for each other, with a similar 1980s warmth.
The original story of young lovers against the odds, in verse, with more feuding and a faster, fatal pace.

h: A shy writer of wizard fan fiction starts college away from her twin sister; sweet, funny and kind to anxious introverts.

like.t: Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda
like.r: Another warm, funny teen story about shyness, online lives and a gentle romance, with a brighter, more playful tone.

like.t: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
like.r: The book whose fandom the heroine writes about, and the cozy, rereadable world this story is built around.
Another funny, awkward and self-doubting narrator slowly finding love and confidence, for an older audience.

t: To All the Boys I've Loved Before
h: A girl's secret love letters are mailed out by accident; a breezy, sweet fake-dating romance with a warm sister story.

like.r: A classic teen romantic comedy of embarrassment and unrequited crushes, with a rougher 1980s edge.
Another funny, awkward first-person narrator in a big-hearted teen comedy, with a royal twist.
A more grounded and more serious teen love story with the same attention to small, shy moments.

t: They Both Die at the End
h: Two strangers are told they will die today and spend their last hours together in New York; sad, tender and oddly life-affirming.

like.r: Another teen love story that faces death head on, trading the near-future premise for a more witty and bookish tone.
Two strangers share one night in a city, talking and falling in love before time runs out, in a quieter and gentler key.

like.t: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
like.r: A more gentle, lyrical teen love story between two boys, about learning to name what you feel.

h: Five students enter detention and one leaves dead; each has a secret worth killing for, in a fast, gossip-laced whodunit.

like.r: The model for five stereotypes locked in a room together, minus the murder and with a far warmer outcome.

like.t: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
like.r: A bright teen amateur sleuth reopens a closed case, in a similarly fast, twisty small-town puzzle.
A modern whodunit with a houseful of suspects with secrets, with more satire and an older cast.

h: A mortal girl raised in the faerie court sets out to win power and ruin her tormentor; scheming, cruel and full of sharp politics.

like.t: A Court of Thorns and Roses
like.r: Another mortal girl pulled into a dangerous faerie realm, with a more romantic and far spicier focus.
A girl in a world of mischievous, risky fae, in a family-friendly musical fantasy with the same glittering menace.
Another ruthless heroine fighting through a court of killers, less political and more action-driven.

h: Cinderella is a cyborg mechanic in New Beijing, and a plague, a prince and a lunar queen close in; inventive and fast.

like.r: A lighter, funnier Cinderella retelling for younger readers, with a curse and a spunky heroine.
A grounded Cinderella without magic, with a sharp heroine, and the same blend of romance and wit.
Another future-set teen story about a resourceful young woman and an unequal society, with a much darker edge.

h: A girl whose touch kills is freed from solitary confinement by a regime that wants a weapon; heated and written in strikethrough poetry.

like.r: Another dystopian teen story of a girl with a dangerous difference, with a more traditional, action-forward style.
A heroine with a surprising power in an unequal world, with a more political story and a love triangle.
A teen dystopia about an engineered society and a girl who sees through it, with more action and less poetry.

h: A red-blooded thief discovers she has silver powers and is hidden at court as a princess; intrigue, betrayals and a divided world.

like.r: The leaner model for a poor girl entering an elite's world and becoming a symbol, with a harsher edge.
Another young woman playing a deadly game in a royal court, with a bigger romance and more magic.
A fast dystopian duel of an elite and an outlaw from the slums, told in alternating voices.

h: Greasers and Socs feud across a mid-60s Oklahoma town, told by a fourteen-year-old poet; raw, sincere and a founding teen novel.

like.r: Another teenage voice at war with the grown-up world, more privileged and wry, less about gangs and loyalty.
The 1950s classic of alienated teens, with the same mix of tough poses and a longing for family.
A short, quiet, elegiac book about friendship and rivalry among boys, set at a boarding school during the war.

h: A freshman stops talking after a summer party no one knows about; her wry, clipped voice carries a painful and hopeful recovery.

like.r: Another teen story of trauma and silence at school, told through tapes and with a darker, more despairing structure.

like.t: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
like.r: A fragile narrator and an undisclosed hurt unfold in a similarly quiet, sad and ultimately hopeful voice.
A memoir of a young woman in a psychiatric hospital, sharing the same sparse candor about a mind in pain.

h: At sixteen everyone is surgically made pretty, and one girl starts asking why; a fast, hoverboard-riding critique of beauty culture.

like.r: A shorter, quieter classic about a comfortable society hiding a price and the child who sees it.
A harder-edged dystopia of a girl against a controlling system, with more violence and higher stakes.
A thoughtful adult film about a society that sorts people by engineered perfection and one man who resists.

h: In a divided, plague-struck Los Angeles a young prodigy hunts the city's most wanted boy; alternating voices and a smart chase.

like.r: The great chase between an inflexible lawman and a hunted outlaw, grown to epic scale and far more serious.
Another teen dystopia of poor against rich, more violent and focused on a single girl's survival.
A sorted-society dystopia that also leans on training, secrets and a looming uprising.

h: A Brooklyn teen witnesses a murder only she can see and meets demon hunters hiding in the city; a swoony monster-of-the-week romp.

like.t: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
like.r: The model for a teen who finds a hidden magical world beside the ordinary one, much lighter and more childlike.
Another supernatural romance for teenagers, with more brooding and less action.
A younger, funnier story of a kid who finds a secret magical world hidden in plain sight.

h: A boy receives seven cassette tapes from a classmate who has died, naming the people who led her there; heavy and compulsive.

like.r: A gentler, more hopeful story of a teen coping with an unspoken harm, told entirely from the survivor's side.

like.t: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
like.r: Another school story of pain and loneliness, with more friendship and a path toward recovery.
Another teen novel about death and what a short life means, with more humor and less guilt.

t: Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda
h: A closeted teen trades anonymous emails with a boy at school while a classmate blackmails him; funny, warm and low on cruelty.

like.t: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
like.r: A more quiet and lyrical story of two boys finding out what they feel, set in a 1980s Mexican-American community.
The warm, glossy film version, which keeps the email mystery and the humor of the book.
Another soft, funny story about shy teenagers and the fear of being seen, with a female lead.

t: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
h: Two Mexican-American boys meet at a swimming pool in 1987 El Paso and slowly learn who they are; spare, gentle and sincere.

like.t: Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda
like.r: A brighter, funnier teen love story about two boys, with email games instead of long summer afternoons.
A grown-up, tragic novel of men learning to name their feelings, more anguished and more adult.
A hushed, intimate portrait of a young man discovering his identity and a bond with another boy, over three stages of life.

h: A klutzy New York ninth grader learns she is the heir to a tiny European throne; told in frantic, funny diary entries.

like.r: The sunny film adaptation, which changes plenty but keeps the makeover comedy and the warmth.
The grown-up diary of an anxious, funny narrator, with the same self-mocking voice and more romance.
The older classic of a spirited, talkative girl who is certain she will never fit in, set in a more sentimental world.

h: Twin artists tell two timelines, three years apart, of the fracture that split them; dreamy, overflowing and highly emotional.

like.t: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
like.r: Another emotional teen story of art, music and friendship, more restrained and plainly told.
A teen tale of love and grief, more witty and plot-driven, less lush and more direct.
A tender teen romance with troubled families in the background, in a more realistic and less lyrical voice.

h: A girl who cannot leave her sealed house falls for the new boy next door; illustrated, quick and built around one large twist.

like.r: Another teen love story shaped by a sick girl and a stubborn boy, with more wit and no big twist.
An adult romance about illness and the limits of what love can fix, with a heavier ending.
A lighter, funnier film that also treats romance as worth risking everything for.

h: Thirty-five girls compete to marry the prince, and a poor girl who never wanted to enter ends up in the finals; The Bachelor in a palace.

like.r: A fairy-tale heroine at court with a prince and secrets, with a richer science-fiction world.
Another girl of the poor classes thrown into a rigged competition at the heart of power, far more brutal.
A feisty commoner falls for a prince in a charming, grounded Cinderella with no magic.

h: A Catholic prep-school boy refuses to sell chocolates for a secret society and is ground down; a famously bleak teen novel.

like.r: A harsher parable of boys, power and cruelty, with the same sense that groups can crush an individual.
A warmer and more sentimental story of teen loyalties, yet with a stark look at gangs and violence.
The solitary prep-school misfit voice, more comic and wandering, less about institutional cruelty.

h: In a society that picks everyone's spouse and job, a girl's match shows two faces; a hushed, poetry-minded dystopian romance.

like.r: The shorter, deeper classic about a society that removes choice, in a similarly quiet voice.
A similar dystopian love story in a world that regards love as a disease, in lush prose.
A more action-driven story with the same question: what is lost when a society removes choice.

h: In a New England where love is a curable disease, a girl days from her procedure falls for a boy outside the fence; lush and aching.

like.r: A neighbouring dystopia where love is controlled, in a more restrained and less passionate telling.
The classic story of a society that removes feeling for safety, in a spare and chilling register.
The original of young love against the world, which this book openly borrows from, in verse and with fewer rules.

h: A bored girl falls down a rabbit hole into a world where logic dissolves into riddles, puns and bad-tempered royalty.

like.r: A bored kid drops into a land built from wordplay and nonsense, with a clearer moral shape and a friendlier tone.
A girl tumbles into a bewildering world of odd rules and eccentric figures, with more beauty and emotional weight.
Another girl who walks through a door into a strange, too-clever world, but darker and much creepier.

h: A chatty orphan with red hair and a huge imagination is mistakenly sent to an elderly pair on Prince Edward Island; warm and funny.

like.r: Another family story of spirited, bookish girls growing up, with a more domestic, moralizing and tearful tone.
Another lonely, strong-willed child who is changed by a home and a garden, with a gentler, mystery-tinged story.
A cheerful orphan transforms a grim household, written with more sweetness and less humor.

h: A sour orphan sent to a Yorkshire manor finds a locked garden and slowly changes herself and two other lonely people.

like.r: The same author's tale of a resilient girl in a bleak household, more focused on imagination and kindness.
A more talkative, comic orphan who wins a household over, with the same sense of healing through place.
A lovely, spooky 1990s film version that leans into the mystery of the house.

h: Three London children fly to an island of pirates and lost boys; sparkling adventure with a surprisingly sad edge about growing up.

like.r: Another Victorian child carried off to a dream-logic land, more absurd and less concerned with time and loss.
An adult Peter Pan returns to Neverland in a big-hearted adventure about the cost of growing up.
A shorter, stranger fable about a boy who never grew up and what adults forget.

h: A mole, a rat, a toad and a badger share riverbanks, picnics and trouble; a gentle, lyrical book about home and friendship.

like.r: Another cozy world of talking animals and friends, simpler and sillier, for a much younger reader.
A far more serious, epic take on a community of animals, with more danger and a mythology of its own.
Talking woodland animals, feasts and loyal friends, but with swordfights and a clearer villain.

h: A bear of very little brain and his friends wander through the Hundred Acre Wood; gentle jokes, gentle sadness, no hurry anywhere.

like.r: A longer, more adult-leaning book of animal friends in the English countryside, with more adventure.
Another barnyard-and-friends story with a gentle voice, but it takes on loss more directly.
A peaceful, soft-edged film of children and gentle forest creatures with no villain in sight.

t: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
h: Four wartime evacuees step through a wardrobe into a land of endless winter; a swift, allegorical battle of good over tyranny.

like.r: A friendlier, funnier quest with a world that feels older, deeper and more detailed.

like.t: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
like.r: A modern child's passage into a hidden magical world, much more focused on school and mystery.
A fairy-tale adventure with great wit and a happier, more mocking tone.

h: A poor boy wins a tour of the world's strangest sweet factory, where greedy children meet comic doom; sugary on top, sharp underneath.

like.r: Another underdog child beating nasty adults, with more heart and a tidier moral.
The classic musical film version, famously eerie, which changes some of the book's details.
Another inventive world full of puns and bizarre rules, with less nastiness and more philosophy.

h: A bookish girl with neglectful parents and a monstrous headmistress finds a surprising power; vicious comedy and genuine warmth.

like.t: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
like.r: Another mistreated child discovering a hidden gift and a kinder world, much longer and more magical.
The faithful and delightfully nasty film version, which relocates the story to America.
Another clever child outwitting horrible adults, funnier, bleaker and deadpan.

h: An orphan snatched from her bed by a gentle giant who blows dreams into children; made up of gloriously mangled words and big laughs.

like.r: Another lonely child flung into a wild adventure with eccentric companions, a bit more dream-like and surreal.
Another story of a kid and a gentle, strange outsider who need each other, with more sentiment.
The ancestor of the invented-word comic tradition, more absurd and without the clear villains.

h: An orphan escapes cruel aunts inside an enormous peach with oversized insect friends, and rolls across the Atlantic; short and zany.

like.r: Another poor boy escapes a hard life into an astonishing place, with a darker joke about greed.
A stop-motion animated Dahl adaptation, with a similar wit and a distinctive look.
The nonsense-adventure parent of this story, with a different sort of absurd and less of an escape plot.

h: A boy and his grandmother learn how to spot witches who hate children; deliciously scary, with an ending that refuses to flinch.

like.r: Another child facing a seemingly friendly creature that wants to harm them, with a creepier, subtler tone.
A gentler Dahl in which a smart child beats nasty adults, with less horror.
A properly frightening film version, with Anjelica Huston's famously terrifying head witch.

h: A runt pig is saved by a barn spider who writes words in her web; a calm, funny, and very moving book about friendship and death.

like.r: The same author's gentler, odder story of a mouse in a human family, with more wandering.
A charming film about a small pig who finds his purpose on a farm, with a similar warm, funny view of animals.
A modern animal friendship story with a similar moving core, told in short, free-verse-like chapters.

h: An awkward girl, her brilliant little brother and a boy cross the universe to find her lost father; odd, earnest and idea-rich.

like.t: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
like.r: Another story of siblings in a larger struggle of good against a creeping darkness, with a more medieval look.
Another child-led odyssey full of strange ideas, wordplay and a loose, brilliant imagination.
Another short, eerie story about conformity and a lone child who resists it, with a quieter setting.

h: A bored boy drives a toy car through a tollbooth into a land where words and numbers are real places; dazzling wordplay.

like.r: The great ancestor of this book, more absurd and less pointed, with the same love of puns and strange logic.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: A grown-up science-fiction comedy of the same breed, with deadpan nonsense and dizzying wordplay.
Another bookish child enters an imaginary world and has to save it, in a deeper and more melancholy tone.

h: The strongest girl in the world lives alone with a horse and a monkey and answers to no adult; anarchic, merry and fearless.

like.r: Another remarkable child who stands up to adult rules, with a sharper, nastier edge to the comedy.
Another spirited, talkative girl who upsets a staid village, with a gentler and more sentimental mood.
A very different but equally free-spirited and memorable child heroine, in a strange and beautiful world.

h: A stranded pilot meets a small boy from a tiny planet who has seen the strange ways of grown-ups; gentle, sad and quotable.

like.r: Another small fable of a strange journey and odd adults, with more nonsense and less tenderness.
Another short fable about the soul, freedom and the courage to be different, with a more spiritual tone.
A film with the same dreamlike strangeness and tender sadness, following a child through a world of odd creatures.

h: A bullied boy steals a book and finds he is part of its story about a dying fantasy land; a book about reading that swallows you.

like.r: A shorter, lighter and funnier tale of a child entering an imaginary land, powered by puns and ideas.
Another book about books coming alive, with a villain and a chase and a very bookish heroine.
Another fairy tale told inside a frame, as a child hears a story, with more laughs and swordplay.

h: A girl discovers a family who drank from a spring and can never die; a slender, golden, sad meditation on living and ending.

like.r: Another short, quiet book that gives a young reader a large moral question without an easy answer.
A children's book that takes death seriously, rooted in friendship and set in a modern rural world.

like.t: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
like.r: A film that treats time and mortality as the central fact of a life, with a similar wistfulness.

h: Two lonely kids invent a secret kingdom in the woods; a short, warm story that turns without warning into a book about grief.

like.r: Another beloved children's book where a friendship is changed by death, in a gentler, funnier barnyard setting.
A boy's bond with his hunting dogs in the Ozarks, equally tearful and rooted in the rural outdoors.
A film about childhood friendship and a first encounter with death, looking back with the same mix of warmth and loss.

h: A boy sent to a Texas camp must dig a hole every day, and old curses and buried secrets start to connect; deadpan and tightly plotted.

like.r: Another tightly built children's puzzle with a cast of odd characters whose stories eventually lock together.
A tougher, leaner survival story of a boy against the elements, with none of the comedy.
A well-liked film version, with the author as screenwriter, that keeps the puzzle-box structure.

h: A lonely ten-year-old adopts a scruffy dog in a Florida supermarket and, through him, gathers a town of lonely friends.

like.r: Another animal-led story of friendship that quietly heals the lonely, with a more classic and pastoral feel.
Another story of a child and a dog, with a far sadder arc and a strong Ozark setting.
Another middle-grade story where an outsider child finds friends, more plot-heavy and wittier.

h: A tiny mouse with big ears falls in love with a princess and goes into the dungeon; an old-fashioned fable narrated with a wink.

like.r: Another medieval-flavored animal world of swords and feasts, with larger battles and far less reflection.
Another fairy tale that talks directly to its audience, with a knowing narrator, true love and real danger.
A small creature's courage and a loving, warm voice, with a barnyard setting and a sadder outcome.

h: A bored girl finds a door to a flat that is almost hers, with button-eyed parents who want to keep her; short, uncanny and scary.

like.r: The stop-motion film version, a rich and disquieting visual treat that follows the book closely.
The classic of a girl walking into an unreal world, far funnier and less menacing.
Another children's book where friendly adults are not what they seem, laced with black humor.

h: A toddler orphaned by a killer is raised by ghosts in a graveyard; a series of eerie, funny episodes that add up to a coming of age.

like.r: The model for this story: a human child raised by non-human guardians, told in a series of linked tales.
The same author's shorter and scarier story of a child in a house of uncanny things.
An animated film that treats the dead as warm companions rather than threats, and is about family and memory.

h: A girl cursed with obedience at birth schemes to break the spell; a fast, funny Cinderella retelling with ogres and elves.

like.r: A darker, more science-fictional take on the Cinderella tale, with an older reader in mind.
A fairy tale that winks at its own conventions and still believes in true love, written for both ages.
A magic-free Cinderella with a stubborn, clever heroine and a sharper, more romantic mood.

h: A boy born with a facial difference enters fifth grade, with chapters told by him, his sister and his classmates; kind and tearful.

like.r: A gentle story of a lonely child and the friends around her, though with a quieter and more Southern tone.
A more plot-driven, funnier story about an outsider boy who finds loyal friends and a place.
A warm and sensitive film version, which keeps the book's many viewpoints and has a lot of heart.

h: A twelve-year-old with ADHD learns he is the son of Poseidon and sets off across America on a quest; wisecracking and nonstop.

like.t: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
like.r: The other great story of a kid learning he belongs to a hidden magical world, slower and more school-based.
A grown-up take on the Greek myths, serious and lyrical, which treats the gods as people rather than punchlines.

like.t: Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief
like.r: The film version, a quicker and flashier take that changes much of the book's plot.

h: Three orphans are handed to a villainous count and warned by their narrator not to read on; gloomy, deadpan and very funny.

like.r: A brighter tale of a clever child against awful adults, with a happier arc and less narrator.
A short, spooky story with a bold child and a sinister adult, but with fewer jokes.
A gothic comic world of dry wit and macabre set design, the film cousin to this story's tone.

h: A self-absorbed middle-schooler narrates a disastrous year in a notebook of stick-figure cartoons; quick, cringey and reluctant-reader friendly.

like.r: Another funny diary by an awkward young narrator, with a girl's perspective and a royal twist.

like.t: The Absolutely True Diary of a Part-Time Indian
like.r: A cartoon-filled first-person teen story, funnier than most and much more emotionally honest and sad.
A distant but fitting cousin of slapstick about a scrappy child outwitting the world, with no words.

h: A thirteen-year-old survives alone in the Canadian wilderness after a plane crash, with nothing but a hatchet; lean and absorbing.

like.r: Another solitary young survivor, based on a true story, with a quieter and more reflective approach.
A boy chooses to live in the woods, a calmer and more idyllic take on the same kind of self-reliance.
The adult film about one person marooned and slowly learning to survive, with the same close focus on tools and fire.

h: Sixteen heirs are paired off to solve the death of an eccentric millionaire; an ingenious, funny and fair-play puzzle.

like.r: The grown-up model of a group of strangers, a mysterious host and a death to solve, far grimmer than this one.
Another children's book in which many odd characters and clues snap together in the end.
A modern film of an eccentric rich family fighting over a will and a death, with a similar playful puzzle structure.

h: A boy in a wolf suit is sent to bed and sails to an island of monsters; ten sentences of wild imagination and home-coming.

like.r: Another picture book of a child drawing his own adventure, quieter and more orderly.
A melancholy film that expands the book into a moody, tactile study of a child's anger.
The long-form ancestor of a child's trip into a strange land and back, with more words and more nonsense.

h: A caterpillar eats its way through a week of increasingly unwise snacks in collage pictures with holes; counting, food and a butterfly.

like.r: Another bedtime-sized picture book built on rhythm and repetition, quieter and more soothing.
Another picture-book classic for small children, wilder and more emotional, with a bigger imagination.

h: Two bored kids and a rain-soaked afternoon meet a tall, mischievous cat who wrecks the house; bouncing rhymes and anarchic fun.

like.r: Another picture book where a child's afternoon becomes a wild adventure, with more mood and imagination.
Another first-reader favorite with a strong rhythm, gentler and based on counting and food.

h: A ten-year-old in occupied Copenhagen helps hide her Jewish best friend and then smuggle her family to safety; spare and suspenseful.

like.r: A longer, more lyrical war story through a girl's eyes, with Death as narrator and a deeper sorrow.

like.t: The Diary of a Young Girl
like.r: The real account of a girl hiding from the Nazis, a first-person document that gives the period its weight.
A film that handles the Holocaust through a child's perspective and a parent's protective love.

t: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH
h: A widowed field mouse seeks help moving her sick son and meets rats made brilliant by laboratory experiments; part fable, part thriller.

like.r: A much longer, tougher animal epic with its own culture and mythology, for older readers.
The darkly beautiful animated version, which adds a magic amulet and a more fantastical look.
Another classic where small animals show remarkable courage, gentler and set entirely on a farm.

h: A silverback gorilla in a shopping-mall circus narrates in short, plain lines how he and an elephant plan to rescue a baby.

like.r: The model for this book: an animal friendship story where kindness changes a creature's fate.
Another modern, warm-hearted book about kindness and being seen, told from a human child's view.
A film about a small animal who changes how everyone around him sees the farm.

h: Mice, hares and badgers defend their abbey against a rat warlord; swordfights, riddles and long, delicious feast descriptions.

like.r: The gentler, more lyrical ancestor of woodland animals with human habits, without the war.
A more serious and epic tale of animals seeking a home, with real mythology and real losses.
A cozy home-loving hero swept into an adventure with songs, food and a dragon.

t: Little House in the Big Woods
h: A girl in a Wisconsin log cabin follows a year of butter-making, bear-scares and fiddle music; a quiet frontier childhood.

like.r: Another warm, domestic girlhood story of the same era, livelier, funnier and set in a more settled village.
A family of spirited sisters and homely virtues, more sentimental and set in a New England town.
Another historically rooted tale of a young person's self-reliance, solitary and more dramatic.

h: A cartoonist interviews his difficult father about surviving Auschwitz, drawing Jews as mice and Nazis as cats; harrowing and humane.

like.r: A calm, precise first-hand account of survival in Auschwitz, in prose rather than pictures, with the same restraint.
Another graphic memoir about a family shaped by political violence, told with more humor and a younger narrator.
The best-known film about the Holocaust, a grand black-and-white drama in contrast to this intimate, wry book.

h: A girl grows up through the Iranian Revolution and the Iran-Iraq war, then in exile in Austria; stark black-and-white panels, wry and defiant.

like.r: Another landmark graphic memoir, about family and political horror, more harrowing and structurally more complicated.
A prose memoir of women in post-revolutionary Iran who find freedom in books, more literary and slower.
The animated film adaptation, which keeps the book's stark drawing style and its sense of humor.

h: Retired, damaged costumed heroes in an alternate 1985 try to solve a murder as nuclear war nears; dense and structurally ambitious.

like.r: The other landmark of the same year, a loud and bruising story of an aging Batman, less layered but just as influential.
A literal, stylized film version which reproduces the panels closely but loses some of the book's inner texture.
A lighter, family-friendly take on retired superheroes and what the world does to them, with cheerful action.

h: A cartoonist circles her bookish, secretive father, a funeral-home director, and her own coming out; precise, literary and sad.

like.r: Another graphic memoir of growing up in a complicated family, with a quicker, more political story.
A prose memoir of a gifted but damaging parent and a child's complex love, more chaotic and less literary.
Another longer graphic memoir about family, faith and first love, softer and more romantic in its handling.

h: The lord of dreams escapes seventy years of captivity and sets out to regain his stolen tools; gothic, mythic and richly strange.

like.r: Another landmark adult comic of its decade, more political and tightly engineered, less dreamy.
A satirical, fantastical novel where the devil appears in modern times, with the same mix of dark wit and myth.
A dark fairy tale for adults, with a similar blend of beauty and cruelty and a gothic sensibility.

h: Two soldiers from warring sides run from both armies with their newborn daughter; baroque, funny, violent and heartfelt.

like.r: The big mythic space opera that Saga takes as its starting point, sunnier and with less sex and gore.

like.t: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
like.r: Another weird, funny and anarchic space tale where the universe runs on bureaucracy, though lighter and more satirical.
The ancestor of two lovers on opposite sides of a feud, here with a happier start and a baby.

h: A masked anarchist wages a theatrical war on a fascist Britain and takes a young woman under his wing; angry and political.

like.r: The totalitarian landscape that this story builds upon, bleaker and more hopeless, with no masked savior.
A slick film adaptation which turns the anarchist politics into more of a conventional action thriller.
A surreal, darkly funny film about a suffocating bureaucratic dystopia, with the same fury at authority.

h: A shapeshifting teenager signs on as a villain's sidekick and torches a medieval-sci-fi kingdom; a quick, funny and surprisingly moving comic.

like.r: Another witty fantasy with a quirky found family, a shapeshifter and a grumpy wizard.
Another warm, funny, queer-friendly graphic novel for young readers, set in a contemporary school.
A film in which a young woman and a flashy wizard share a magical, whimsical, found family.

h: A shy schoolboy and a rugby player at an English school become friends and then more; soft, sweet, and very fast to read.

like.t: Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda
like.r: Another sweetly funny teen story of a boy navigating a first crush, told in prose.

like.t: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
like.r: A quieter, more lyrical love story between two teenage boys, with deeper family and identity themes.
A film with the same warm tone, about a closeted teen and an anonymous crush.

h: A boy raised in a strict evangelical home falls for a girl at winter church camp; a long, snowy, aching memoir in brush ink.

like.r: Another graphic memoir about a complicated family and growing up, more literary and more grown-up.
Another coming-of-age memoir in black and white, funnier and political, with a stronger outsider's voice.

like.t: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
like.r: A shy, sensitive teen narrator finds love and friends, with the same yearning and sadness.

h: Biker gangs and psychic children collide in a Neo-Tokyo rebuilt after catastrophe; huge, kinetic and densely drawn.

like.r: The landmark animated film, a compressed and overwhelming version of the first half of the manga.
The founding cyberpunk novel, a hard-boiled, neon-lit tale of tech and criminals, with less action.
Another neon-lit city of the future, more contemplative and noir-like, with less destruction.

h: A grey, retired Bruce Wayne straps on the cowl again in a crime-ridden Gotham; brutal, bitter and the root of grim superhero tales.

like.r: The subtler, more tightly built companion of the same year, which questions heroes rather than celebrating them.
A crime saga of Gotham, with a similar bleak view of the hero and the city but more realistic.
An earlier gothic film version, less brutal and more theatrical.

h: Two sardonic, newly graduated friends drift apart through a bland American town; deadpan, small and sad.

like.r: The wry film adaptation, with Thora Birch and Steve Buscemi, which expands the story but keeps its sour charm.
The original disaffected narrator who finds everything phony, more talkative and less cartoonish.
Another black-and-white story of a sharp-tongued girl growing up, warmer and with higher stakes.

h: After a fall that wrecks her front teeth, a sixth grader spends years in braces and through changing friends; friendly and funny.

like.r: Another middle-school story about how it feels to look different, in prose and with a kind of group chorus.
Another illustrated middle-school book, more cynical and goofy.
A more serious and political graphic memoir of growing up, for older readers.

h: A brilliant student finds a notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it, and a genius detective hunts him; a mind duel.

like.r: The classic of a clever young man who believes he stands above the law, far deeper and more psychological.
Another bleak thriller about a killer with a moral mission and the detectives chasing him.
A battle of wits between an investigator and a brilliant, dangerous mind.
